title: Hermetic browser and scrape evals in CI through the production tool contract, with injection and ZDR fixtures and per-release scores
summary: Extend the existing in-process TestSite and lab/evals fixtures with prompt-injection pages and ZDR cases, add record/replay of driver HTTP and CDP exchanges (path-confined fixtures), and add a CI job that runs lab/evals on a labelled PR and after each deploy, writing the SCOREBOARD with the commit SHA. As a later increment on canary.rs, add a mirror-and-diff mode for non-ZDR, consenting, non-agent traffic. || Drive the existing browser benchmark corpus through the same path production uses (Model Plane browser.observe and act tools, BrowserBroker grant, quarry-edge agent routes) against recorded fixture sites, score task success, steps and cost, and publish the result per release in CI.
whyItMatters: It keeps parity claims honest and catches regressions in driver escalation, ZDR behaviour and prompt-injection handling before users do. The harness is already substantial, but every scoreboard suite is pending and CI does not run it. || Agent quality regressions are caught before release only if evals exercise the real contract. Quarry's scoreboard is all pending and the Python eval-lab targets model-gateway, so the browser agent is currently benchmarked in neither place end to end.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (controlled test site with e2e snips gated by environment, CI matrix over engine, proxy and queue backends, mock record/replay, evals on a PR hashtag and after deploy)
others: Firecrawl shadow traffic: sampled mirror or split to staging, skipped for ZDR and agent jobs, outputs compared asynchronously
Codex in-app browser (same runtime archives used by training and production)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl); unique || 1 of 4 sources; unique (documentation only)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Serve a fixture site in CI and run e2e tests through the gateway; record mode writes driver exchanges to JSON fixtures and replay serves them by name; a CI job runs evals on a labelled PR and after deploy. Mirror mode: with probability r and only for consenting non-ZDR tenants, enqueue a job to the candidate driver, compare markdown similarity and latency, and store the result in an experiments table. || Merged items add: The eval harness installs the same CI-published runtime version as production and drives the same tool contract against a training browser service, so scores are comparable across releases.

verevonToday.gap: A Rust eval harness exists (bakeoff, browser_benchmark, provider_matrix, release_matrix, web_rerank_gate) with 12 HTML fixtures and a local TestSite (landing, login, gated dashboard, search), but every scoreboard suite is pending, quarry-v2-ci.yml runs cargo test only (no lab/evals job), and there is no record/replay and no prompt-injection or ZDR fixture. Canary splitting and experiment tagging are shipped; there is no mirror-and-diff mode. || SRC: Quarry lab/evals has a browser benchmark, a deterministic test site and a release-matrix binary, but the scoreboard suites are all pending. The Python eval-lab runs selftests in CI and live evals only against model-gateway with credentials. Nothing drives Model Plane browser.observe/act against quarry-edge with fixtures, so it is not established that evals cover the production tool contract.

approach: [R-t2-07-10] Ingestion Plane: add injection and ZDR pages to TestSite and lab/evals/fixtures, add a record/replay layer for driver exchanges, and wire lab/evals into a GitHub workflow triggered by a PR label and by deploy, publishing SCOREBOARD automatically. Mirror mode in canary.rs is optional and follows once evals exist; it must skip ZDR and agent runs. || [R-t2-06-10] Ingestion Plane lab/evals: add a runner that starts quarry-edge with the test site and a stub BrowserBroker, replays recorded planner traces or a fixed small model through the Model Plane tool protocol, and emits task-success, steps and cost; add it to the quarry-v2 CI workflow as a non-live job and to a scheduled live job. Publish release_matrix output with the new scores; use recorded fixtures instead of live sites to avoid flakiness.
risks: Flaky live-site evals (run live evals only after deploy); mirroring doubles third-party load and needs consent and ZDR exclusion. || Flaky live-site benchmarks (use recorded fixtures); model cost for live evals; CI runner limits for Chromium (the quarry-v2 workflow already documents build instability).

verevon.exactGap: lab/evals (quarry-eval, bakeoff, provider_matrix, release_matrix, web_rerank_gate, plus a checked-in 10/10 fixture scoreboard.json dated 2026-05-08) is a workspace member whose unit tests run in cargo test --workspace, but no workflow runs its binaries, the docs/SCOREBOARD.md comparison suites are all pending, and its 'browser benchmark' is a mock-driver preview-latency microbenchmark rather than a task-success corpus. TestSite has no consumer, canary.rs and experiments.rs are unwired dead-code scaffolding (not shipped), there are no injection fixtures or record/replay, and live Chromium tests self-skip because CHROMIUMOXIDE_TEST is set in no workflow. Execution-core does already have a real end-to-end test (tests/browser_agent_e2e.rs: Model Plane loop to QuarryAgentClient to quarry-edge to Chromium) with fixture-based planner probe cases, but it is #[ignore]d for needing a live stack and does no scoring, and ZDR rejection is already covered deterministically by quarry-edge/tests/zdr_behavior.rs and zdr_claim_floor.rs.

verevon.constraints: Prompt-injection screening is a Model Plane duty (execution-core provenance.rs, model-gateway moderation/semantic screening), so a Quarry-only fixture can prove only that hostile text is returned unmodified; an injection eval must include the Model Plane render seam. ZDR fixtures should assert no artifact, cache, checkpoint or timeline writes. The quarry-v2 CI already documents Chromium-link disk crashes, so browser evals belong in a labelled or scheduled job, hermetic via TestSite and recorded fixtures, with live-model evals only after deploy. No cross-plane DB access: the harness talks to quarry-edge over HTTP like production.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Phase 0 (S): add a quarry-v2-ci job that runs quarry-eval, quarry-bakeoff and release_matrix and uploads scoreboard with the commit SHA. Phase 1 (M): make browser_agent_e2e hermetic (quarry-edge with the browser-agent feature plus a stub grant validator against TestSite, deterministic planner or recorded planner traces) and score success, steps and cost; add injection pages to TestSite and assert on the Model Plane screening verdict; add ZDR no-write assertions. Drop the canary mirror-and-diff clause: canary.rs and experiments.rs are unwired scaffolding, so it would be a separate feature. Correct the description: the 'browser benchmark corpus' is a preview-latency microbenchmark, not tasks.
verevon.effortNote: Phase 0 is S and phase 1 M; with record/replay and the production-contract harness the whole item is L, not M.
verevon.verdictReason: The harness pieces exist but nothing runs in CI and the item mislabels canary/experiments as shipped, the browser benchmark as a task corpus, and misses the existing ignored real e2e test and the ZDR tests; scope and effort need correcting.
